stem_book: Passage Q.(i) to (v). Concrete is produced from a mixture of cement, water and small stones. A small amount of gypsum, CaSO₄·2H₂O, is added in cement production to improve the subsequent hardening of concrete. The elevated temperature during cement production may lead to formation of unwanted hemihydrate: CaSO₄·2H₂O(s) → CaSO₄·(1/2)H₂O(s) + (3/2)H₂O(g). ΔfH° of CaSO₄·2H₂O(s), CaSO₄·(1/2)H₂O(s), H₂O(g) are −2021.0, −1575.0 and −241.8 kJ mol⁻¹; their standard entropies are 194.0, 130.0 and 188.0 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹. R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹ = 0.0831 L bar mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. (i) Heat change during conversion of 1 kg of CaSO₄·2H₂O(s) (molar mass 172 g mol⁻¹) to CaSO₄·(1/2)H₂O(s) is (a) 484 kJ (b) 400 kJ (c) −484.0 kJ (d) −1000 kJ. (ii) ΔG° for the reaction at 298 K is (a) 120 kJ mol⁻¹ (b) 17.92 kJ mol⁻¹ (c) −180 kJ mol⁻¹ (d) 10 kJ mol⁻¹. (iii) The equilibrium constant is (a) ≈ 0 (b) < 1 (c) > 1 (d) = 1. (iv) The equilibrium pressure of water vapour in a closed vessel containing CaSO₄·2H₂O(s), CaSO₄·(1/2)H₂O(s) and H₂O(g) at 298 K (antilog −3.14 = 7.24×10⁻⁴) is (a) (17.24×10⁻⁴) bar (b) (−7.24×10⁻⁴)³ bar (c) (18×10⁻⁴)^(2/3) bar (d) (7.24×10⁻⁴)^(2/3) bar. (v) The formation of CaSO₄·(1/2)H₂O at 298 K is (a) Spontaneous (b) Endothermic and non-spontaneous (c) Exothermic and non-spontaneous (d) None of these
reason: Five-part passage under one code (separate answers). Keys verified; note exact ΔG° = 18.34 kJ (printed option 17.92 is the nearest and is what (iv)'s antilog −3.14 uses).
